name: Shipment Approval
description: Sequential approval chain for high-value or non-standard shipments. Dispatcher raises the request; Operations Manager reviews; if value exceeds 500 the CEO must co-sign. Exercises: sequential chain + CEL conditional branch. Escalation follows D-ESC: timer -> higher role -> fail closed (v1.4, ISS-1007 / Q-989; BA ruling GH #2281). Every human task carries the escalation_timer_duration + escalation_role pair; when the timer fires the engine cancels the task and follows the node's single unconditioned (timeout) edge. Chain: ops-review (role-ops-manager, PT2H, the existing E7 exception) -> ceo-approval (role-ceo, PT4H) -> stalled: auto-reject, never release-shipment. Deviations (documented, no waivers): ceo-approval takes PT4H rather than the financial P2D because a shipment awaiting co-signature is time-sensitive operational work, consistent with ops-review's PT2H. ceo-approval is the top of the chain (E4): its escalation_role repeats its own role as a nominal CHK-21 co-required attribute and its timeout edge goes straight to the fail-closed auto-reject. Decision forms (v1.5, ISS-1008 / Q-990): ops-review and ceo-approval each carry a form_schema with a required, enumerated (approve, reject) decision field named exactly as the outgoing edges read it (ops_decision, ceo_decision), and declared_value, which the value gateway reads, is a required start input typed as a number by variable_schemas. Limitations (documented, not waived): form_schema is a UI rendering payload only (REQ-273) and the engine's variable_schemas check validates only the variables a completion submits, so a null or out-of-enum decision is rejected server-side but a completion that omits the decision key is not: it fails closed (ops-review then goes to ceo-approval, ceo-approval then goes to auto-reject, never release-shipment). The node model has no start form, so declared_value is required by convention of the instance creation request, not by a form. Required decision outputs (v1.6, REQ-462 / Q-1025, REQ-459 design): ops-review declares required_outputs [ops_decision] and ceo-approval declares required_outputs [ceo_decision], each with a variable_schema, so a completion that omits the decision key is now refused with a retryable 422 (output_refused, missing_keys), the task stays open and the instance is unchanged; this supersedes the omitted-key limitation stated above (the null / out-of-enum rejection is unchanged). Separation of duties (v1.7, REQ-466 / Q-1029, GH #2344): ceo-approval may not be decided by the person who completed ops-review on the same shipment.

ops_decision.title: Operations decision
ops_decision.description: Operations Manager review of the shipment. 'approve' sends it on (to the CEO co-sign when the declared value exceeds 500, otherwise to release); 'reject' rejects it and notifies the requester. The routing reads this field.

attributes.description: top of chain: escalation_role is nominal; stalled = fail closed

ceo_decision.title: CEO decision
ceo_decision.description: CEO co-signature for a shipment above 500. 'approve' releases the shipment; 'reject' rejects it. The routing reads this field; leaving it unset fails closed to auto-reject.
